text:
jg_corp: Hey team — since yesterday ~30% of our API calls to api.jgc.example.com are failing with `tls: handshake failure` when sent from our prod VPC via the interface endpoint. curl -v shows handshake aborts. No changes on our side. Can we escalate?

maria_support: sorry you're hitting this, we're on it. Can you paste the curl -v output and confirm whether you're using the VPCE private DNS name or a custom CNAME?

jg_corp: here's a minimal repro from an app host: `curl -v https://api.jgc.example.com/health -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"` -> sometimes succeeds, sometimes: `* TLS handshake, TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS alert, Client hello (1)` `* SSL: certificate subject name (api.jgc.example.com) does not match target host name '54.210.1.23'` so it looks like DNS is returning a public IP occasionally.

sanjay_eng: that error is telling — if DNS is resolving to a public IP the request will egress internet instead of going to the interface endpoint ENI. Do you have a Route53 private hosted zone for jgc.example.com in your VPC? That can cause split-horizon issues if records point to public ip/ALB.

jg_corp: we do have a private hosted zone we put in last quarter to manage some internal names. I assumed the VPCE private DNS would take precedence.

maria_support: two quick checks: `dig +short api.jgc.example.com` from an app host and `getent hosts api.jgc.example.com`. Also check `nslookup api.jgc.example.com <VPC resolver IP>` (usually .2). If you see public IPs there, PHZ is the culprit.

jg_corp: dig result flips between private IPs (10.0.4.23) and public 54.210.1.23 depending on the host. traceroute shows hops to IGW when it returns 54.210.1.23.

sanjay_eng: yep. root cause: private hosted zone record is shadowing the VPCE private DNS. When DNS resolves to public IP traffic leaves VPC and handshake fails because SNI/cert is for domain but endpoint IP belongs to ALB/NLB public listener. Two fixes: (1) remove conflicting record(s) from your PHZ so the interface endpoint's private DNS resolves to its ENI IPs; (2) if you must keep PHZ, create A records that point to the VPCE ENI IPs (not public) or use CNAME to the vpce-specific hostnames returned by AWS, and ensure private DNS on the VPCE is enabled.

jg_corp: we enabled private dns on the VPCE during setup. How do we map PHZ records to the ENI IPs reliably? ENI IPs can move on scaling.

sanjay_eng: don't hardcode ENI IPs. Better approach: delete the PHZ entries for api.jgc.example.com and let the VPCE private DNS override. If you need custom records, create an ALIAS in the PHZ pointing to the AWS VPCE endpoint service (if supported) or use the regional vpce DNS name AWS provides (example: `vpce-xxxxxxxx-abcdef.vpce-svc-xxxxxxxx.region.vpce.amazonaws.com`) as a CNAME so the platform resolves to current ENIs. Another option: create a private hosted zone in the account that hosts the endpoint service and share it (if multi-account).

maria_support: also confirm security group on the interface endpoint allows inbound 443 from your subnets and that your app subnets have no egress rule overriding traffic. Example SG check: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=vpce-*/ --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].Groups'` — confirm group allows your CIDR.

jg_corp: SG was fine, but we found an old PHZ record created as an A -> public ALB IP from a migration. We removed the PHZ record and forced DNS flush on the hosts. After that our curl samples stably return 200.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: noted DNS change in jg-corp account at 2025-11-03T15:34:02Z (PHZ record deleted).

tim_oncall: recommend following up with the customer to validate no intermittent hits remain and to run a 1k-req smoke test. Also suggest adding a healthcheck route that hits `/health` with SNI to verify certs present.

jg_corp: ran 1k requests, 0 failures now. Thanks for the fast help. We'll avoid putting service names in PHZ unless necessary and will use CNAME -> vpce hostnames for future migrations. :thumbsup:

maria_support: great — closing this thread, please reopen if it reappears and paste tcpdump + `dig +trace` outputs for deeper analysis. :white_check_mark:
